## Layer `Infrastructure`

This directory contains the `Infrastructure` layer. Infrastructure holds the data access implementations and the services that interact with infrastructure concerns, implementing interfaces defined in the Application Core. Its architecture rules:

- `layering/infrastructure-not-ui` — The Infrastructure layer must not reference the Web layer, the PublicApi layer or the BlazorAdmin layer. Infrastructure implements interfaces defined in the Application Core. Both the UI and Infrastructure depend on the Application Core, and Infrastructure has no reason to know a UI exists. See <https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/architecture/modern-web-apps-azure/common-web-application-architectures>.
- `layering/infrastructure-not-blazor-shared` — Some existing code here still follows the OLD pattern: The identity seed reads role names from BlazorShared.Authorization.Constants. That is grandfathered debt, not house style. New code must follow: The Infrastructure layer must not reference the BlazorShared layer. Infrastructure implements the Application Core's interfaces, and BlazorShared is the admin client's contract with the API. Infrastructure reaches BlazorShared only through the Application Core's project reference to it. See <https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/architecture/modern-web-apps-azure/common-web-application-architectures>. If you are already editing a grandfathered site and the migration is small, migrate it; otherwise do not grow the debt.
- Expand any rule above with `sliderule explain <rule-id>`.

## Cautioned scope `infrastructure/ef-migrations`

This directory contains the cautioned `infrastructure/ef-migrations` scope: types in `Microsoft.eShopWeb.Infrastructure.Data.Migrations.*` or `Microsoft.eShopWeb.Infrastructure.Identity.Migrations.*`. Here be dragons: the weirdness below is structural; read it before you edit, and do not tidy it away.

Dragons: EF Core migrations for CatalogContext and AppIdentityDbContext, generated by `dotnet ef migrations add`. Each migration is history already applied to existing databases: editing or deleting one desynchronises them from the code, and the *.Designer.cs files and *ModelSnapshot.cs are tool output that the next migration diffs against. Change the model, then add a new migration with the commands in the README; never hand-edit an existing one.

- `infrastructure/ef-migrations/tripwire` — a change set touching this scope is flagged by `check --diff-base <ref>`. Migrations are generated history that existing databases have already applied.
- Expand: `sliderule explain infrastructure/ef-migrations/tripwire`.
